angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 731,876 km at 142.64 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0108 +/- 0.0124 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 142.64 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.052 +/- 0.012 solar radii from Barragán et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-837 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.531.4275B/abstract): 731,876 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.142 +/- 0.008 solar masses from Barragán et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-837 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.531.4275B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5995 +/- 79 K from Barragán et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-837 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.531.4275B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Barragán et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-837 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.531.4275B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-837.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.452, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
